features.feature_value: Threatenability/feasibility frame via parallel 'question isn't whether X exists' construction; mirror shifts X from Second Amendment to voting rights
features.evidence_span: "The question isnt whether the Second Amendment exists. Its whether regular people can realistically exercise it."
features.rationale: Uses a repeated 'question isn't whether X' pattern with a feasibility qualifier, and the mirror retargets the same structure to voting rights.

features.feature_value: Risk of government retaliation discouraging lawful exercise
features.evidence_span: "Without fear of their government coming after them."
features.rationale: Explicitly ties ability to exercise rights to fear of state enforcement.

features.feature_value: Direct insult + corruption analogy using 'damn dumb' and 'Orangutan in Chief' label
features.evidence_span: "How are Texas Republicans this damn dumb??? Paxton is a more corrupt version of the Orangutan in Chief"
features.rationale: Uses highly contemptuous insults and a pejorative animal/derogatory comparison to delegitimize targeted actors.

features.feature_value: Profanity embedded in attribution; rhetorical retargeting from capital police to border agents
features.evidence_span: "Trump to the capital police \"Fuck you, my rioters are all I care about, not you\"."
features.rationale: Contains explicit taboo language and quote-style attribution that sets up a blame/priority contrast.

features.feature_value: Mirror shifts blame from handling domestic 'rioters' to immigration enforcement vs 'open borders agenda'
features.evidence_span: "Biden to the border patrol agents: 'Fuck you, my open borders agenda is all I care about, not you.'"
features.rationale: The mirror clearly re-targets the same communicative 'who you care about' framing to a different political issue and actor group.

features.feature_value: Women's right to choose clothing; policing framed as domination/control; 'Very feminist' vs 'Very pro-life' mirror tag
features.evidence_span: "women shouldn't have this choice. They need to cover the fuck up!"
features.rationale: Centers a culture-war subject (women's autonomy) with strong moral/political framing.

features.feature_value: Second-person conditional argument about who is 'interested' in 'cooming' / control of female bodies
features.evidence_span: "If you think shorts are appropriate for a woman to wear you're just interested in cooming."
features.rationale: Uses an 'If you think...' persuasive challenge addressed to the reader, coupled with accusatory motivation language.

features.feature_value: Ideological causal claims + policy prescription via quoted generalization and 'job of any govt is to...'
features.evidence_span: "Socialists are the destroyers of any economy in the world, and they're the enablers of public corruption"..."the job of any govt is to regulate"
features.rationale: Employs an economy-wide causal claim about ideologies and follows with an explicit government role prescription; mirror swaps to the opposite ideological thesis.
